title: 2026 Roadmap on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Smart Manufacturing
summary: An 83-page peer-reviewed roadmap surveys AI and machine-learning foundations, application areas, and emerging techniques for smart manufacturing while identifying persistent data, integration, reliability, interpretability, and scale barriers.
key_findings: The roadmap organizes the field around foundations and trends, application domains such as sensing, autonomous systems, additive manufacturing, digital twins, robotics, supply chains, and sustainability, and emerging methods such as physics-informed, generative, semantic, and foundation-model approaches.

It identifies noisy or incomplete industrial data, heterogeneous sensing and control systems, limited interpretability, domain shift, real-time performance, and multi-factory scalability as continuing deployment constraints.
It treats trustworthy operation, reliability, availability, maintainability, safety, and data-centric metrology as necessary components of industrial AI rather than optional overlays.
why_it_matters: The roadmap gives FTFN a current, technically detailed research-priority map for separating promising AI-for-manufacturing methods from the integration and assurance work required for dependable factory use.
ftfn_relevance: Strengthens Advanced Manufacturing and AI for Science with a current peer-reviewed foundation.
Names concrete dependency lanes for metrology, data infrastructure, interoperability, reliability, safety, and scale evidence.
Supports later searches for testbeds, standards, pilots, factory validation, and production outcomes.
evidence_limits: The paper is a research roadmap, not a deployment census or product evaluation.
It does not prove that a named factory has integrated, validated, or scaled the reviewed approaches.
Forward-looking research directions and expected 2025-2035 developments remain scenarios rather than delivered capabilities.
